answer: Topological Rarity Scoring. Each agent's trust weight is the inverse frequency of its neighborhood signature—its pattern of connections to distinct clusters. Genuine agents sit in varied positions like trees in an orchard, each root network unique. A sybil farm clones one signature across many nodes, so the signature's rarity collapses and all copies drop toward zero weight. A beacon node flagging a dense cluster triggers recursive downweighting, and a reef of mutually-reinforcing fakes cannot raise its own score since signatures stay identical.
